Dear Ms. Reyes,

We are writing about your claim for benefits from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

**We could not approve your claim yet.** We asked you for a certified copy of your marriage license. We sent that request in a letter dated June 3, 2024. We have not received it. Because of this, we have denied your claim for now.

**You can still send us the paper.** You can send it at any time. But please try to send it by June 3, 2025. That is one year after our first letter. If we get it after that date, and you qualify for benefits, we can only pay you from the day we get the paper. We cannot pay you for the time before that.

**If you disagree with our decision,** you may have a right to appeal. You may think the papers we already have are enough to approve your claim. If so, please read the form we included with this letter. It is called VA Form 1-4107, *Notice of Procedural and Appellate Rights*. It explains how to appeal.

Sincerely,

[Name]
Department of Veterans Affairs

**Notice: Medicare Will Stop Paying for Your Home Health Care**

Patient name: Walter Pruitt

**Medicare will stop paying for your home health care on Friday, March 14, 2025.**

Your provider or health plan decided that Medicare will probably not pay for your home health care after that date. If you keep getting care after that date, you may have to pay for it yourself.

**Your right to appeal**

You have the right to appeal this decision. An appeal means asking an independent reviewer to look at it again.

- If you appeal, your care will keep going while the review happens.
- The reviewer will ask for your opinion. You do not have to write anything down, but you can if you want to.
- The reviewer will also look at your medical records and other information about your care.
- After you ask for an appeal, you will get a written letter that explains in detail why your care coverage should end.
- If the reviewer agrees that Medicare should stop paying, neither Medicare nor your health plan will pay for your care after March 14, 2025.
- If you stop getting care by March 14, 2025, you will not have to pay for it.

**How to ask for an appeal right away**

- Ask as soon as you can. Your request must be made no later than noon on the day before March 14, 2025.
- Send your request to your Quality Improvement Organization, or QIO. A QIO is the independent reviewer that Medicare approves.
- Call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142 to ask for an appeal or to ask questions.
- If you miss the deadline, you may still have the right to appeal.

**What happens next**

- The QIO will tell you its decision as soon as possible. This is usually within two days after March 14, 2025.
- If you have a Medicare health plan, the QIO will usually tell you its decision by March 14, 2025.
- To learn more, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142.

## Medicare will stop paying for your home health care on Friday, March 14, 2025.

Your care provider or health plan thinks Medicare most likely will not pay for your home health care after this date. If you keep getting care after March 14, 2025, you may have to pay for it yourself.

## You have the right to appeal

An appeal means you ask for this decision to be looked at again. You have the right to appeal the decision to stop Medicare coverage.

- An outside medical expert will review your case right away. This expert does not work for us.
- Your care will keep going while the review is happening.
- The reviewer will ask what you think. You do not have to write anything down. But you have the right to write down your thoughts if you want to.
- The reviewer will also look at your medical records and any other facts that matter.
- After you ask for an appeal, you will get a notice. It will explain in detail why your coverage should end.
- If the reviewer agrees that Medicare should stop paying on March 14, 2025, then neither Medicare nor your health plan will pay for care after that date.
- If you stop your care by March 14, 2025, you will not have to pay for it.

## How to ask for a fast appeal

- Ask as soon as you can.
- **Your deadline is noon (12:00 p.m.) on Thursday, March 13, 2025.** That is the day before your coverage ends.
- Make your request to your Quality Improvement Organization. This is called a "QIO." The QIO is the outside reviewer that Medicare approves.
- If you miss the deadline, you may still have the right to appeal.
- To appeal, or if you have questions, call your QIO:
  **Midsouth Quality Review: 1-888-555-0142**

- The QIO will tell you its decision as soon as it can. This is usually no later than 2 days after March 14, 2025.

# Medicare May Not Pay for Your Test
This is an Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage (ABN).

Medicare does not pay for everything. This is true even for some care that you or your health care provider think you need.

We think Medicare may not pay for the test listed below. If Medicare does not pay, you may have to pay.

- **Test:** Vitamin D blood test
- **Why Medicare may not pay:** Medicare usually pays for this test only once every 12 months.
- **Estimated cost:** $187.50

# What to Do Now
1. Read this notice. It will help you make an informed choice about your care.
2. Ask us any questions you have.
3. Choose one option below. Tell us if you still want the test.

**Choose only ONE option. We can't choose for you.**

If you choose Option 1 or Option 2, we may help you use any other insurance you have. But Medicare can't make us do this.

## Option 1: Get the test, and Medicare is billed
- I want the vitamin D blood test.
- I want Medicare to be billed. Medicare will make an official decision about payment. I will get that decision on a Medicare Summary Notice (MSN).
- You can ask me to pay now.
- If Medicare does not pay, I am responsible for paying.
- I can appeal to Medicare. I do this by following the directions on the MSN.
- If Medicare does pay, you will give back any money I paid you. You will keep only my co-pays or deductibles.

## Option 2: Get the test, and Medicare is not billed
- I want the vitamin D blood test.
- Do not bill Medicare.
- You can ask me to pay now.
- I am responsible for paying.
- I can't appeal, because Medicare is not billed.

## Option 3: Do not get the test
- I do not want the vitamin D blood test.
- I am not responsible for paying.
- I can't appeal to find out if Medicare would pay.

This letter is **not** the decision on your appeal. The decision on your appeal will come from your Quality Improvement Organization (QIO).

Dear Harold Vance,

This letter is about your stay at Maury Regional Hospital. Please read it carefully.

**Your rights as a patient**

- You can get services that Medicare covers. This includes hospital care that you need for your health. You have the right to know which services are covered.
- You can work with the hospital to get ready to leave safely. The hospital can also help you set up any care you will need after you go home. If you have questions or worries, you can talk with your doctor or other hospital staff.
- If you have concerns about the care you are getting, you can contact the group that checks the quality of hospital care. It is called Midsouth Quality Review. Call them at 1-888-555-0142. This group is separate from Medicare.

**If you think you are being sent home too soon**

- You can ask to appeal. An appeal means asking someone to look again at the decision. You can do this right away.
- To appeal, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142.
- Ask for your appeal as soon as you can, and before you leave the hospital. If you ask before you leave, Medicare will keep paying for your hospital stay while you wait for the decision.
- If you ask for an appeal, Midsouth Quality Review will look at your records. They will give you their decision in about 2 days.
- You can still appeal after you leave the hospital. If you have Original Medicare, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142. If you have a Medicare Advantage plan, call your plan at Volunteer Advantage Plan at 1-877-555-0175.

**What happens after you appeal**

- If you appeal, you will get another paper called a Detailed Notice of Discharge. It explains why the hospital thinks your covered stay should end.
- If the appeal decision is in your favor, Medicare will keep paying for your hospital care.
- If you do not appeal, or if the decision is not in your favor, you may have to pay for care you get after your discharge date.

**Please sign this letter** to show that you got it and understand it.

**Other help you can get**

You have the right to get Medicare information in a format that is easier to read or hear, such as large print, braille, or audio. # An Important Message from Medicare

## Your Rights as a Hospital Patient

- **Medicare helps pay for your care.** This includes hospital care that you need for your health. You have the right to know what Medicare covers.
- **You can help plan your trip home.** The hospital will work with you to make sure it is safe for you to leave. They can also help set up any care you may need after you go home. If you are worried about anything, talk to your doctor or the hospital staff.
- **You can report problems with your care.** If you are not happy with the quality of your care, call this group: Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142. This group is not part of Medicare. It is separate.

## You Can Appeal if You Are Sent Home Too Soon

An appeal is a way to ask for a second look at a decision.

- If you think the hospital wants you to leave too soon, you can appeal right away.
- To appeal, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142.
- Call as soon as you can. Be sure to call **before you leave the hospital**. If you appeal before you leave, Medicare will keep paying for your stay while you wait to hear the answer.
- If you appeal, the group will look at your records. They will tell you their answer in about 2 days.
- You can still appeal after you leave the hospital.
  - If you have Original Medicare, call Midsouth Quality Review.
  - If you have a Medicare Advantage plan, call your plan. Your plan is Volunteer Advantage Plan. The phone number is 1-877-555-0175.

## What Happens After I Appeal?

- You will get another letter called the **Detailed Notice of Discharge**. It tells you why the group thinks you no longer need to stay in the hospital.
- If the answer is **yes** (they agree with you), Medicare will keep paying for your hospital care.
- If you **do not appeal**, or if the answer is **no**, you may have to pay for any care you get after your discharge date.

## Please Sign

- You can ask for Medicare information in another form. Choices include large print, braille, or audio.
- If you feel someone treated you unfairly, you have the right to make a complaint.
- To learn more, go to Medicare.gov/about-us/accessibility-nondiscrimination-notice. You can also call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227).
- If you use a TTY phone, call 1-877-486-2048.

## An Important Message from Medicare

## Your Rights While You Are Staying in the Hospital

- Medicare pays for some of your care. This includes hospital care that your doctor says you need. You have the right to know what Medicare will pay for.
- You can work with the hospital to plan for when you go home. This helps you leave safely. The hospital can also help you set up any care you need after you leave. If you are worried about anything, talk to your doctor or another hospital worker.
- Do you have a problem with the care you are getting? You can tell a group that checks on hospital care. This group is called a Quality Improvement Organization. Yours is Midsouth Quality Review. Call them at 1-888-555-0142. This group is not part of Medicare.

## You Can Ask for a Review If You Think You Are Leaving Too Soon

- Leaving the hospital is called being "discharged." If you think the hospital is sending you home too soon, you can ask for a review right away. This is called an "appeal."
- To ask for a review, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142.
- Call as soon as you can. Try to call before you leave the hospital. If you call before you leave, Medicare will keep paying for your stay while you wait for an answer.
- Midsouth Quality Review will look at your records. They will give you an answer about 2 days after you call.
- You can still ask for a review after you leave the hospital.
  - If you have Original Medicare, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142.
  - If you have a Medicare Advantage plan, call Volunteer Advantage Plan at 1-877-555-0175.

## What Happens After I Ask for a Review?

- You will get another letter. It is called the "Detailed Notice of Discharge." It will tell you why the hospital and your plan think your stay should end.
- If the review goes your way, Medicare will keep paying for your hospital care.
- If you do not ask for a review, or if the review does not go your way, you may have to pay for care you get after the day you were supposed to leave.

# Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage

**Patient name:** Walter Pruitt

## Your Medicare coverage for home health care is ending

Medicare coverage of your home health services from Riverbend Home Health will end on **Friday, March 14, 2025**.

Your provider or health plan decided that Medicare probably will not pay for your home health services after that date. You may have to pay for any services you get after March 14, 2025.

## You have the right to appeal

You can appeal the decision to end your Medicare coverage. If you appeal:

- You get an independent medical review right away.
- Your services continue while the appeal is going on.
- The independent reviewer will ask for your opinion.
- You do not have to write anything down. But you have the right to prepare a written statement if you want to.
- The reviewer will also look at your medical records and other useful information.
- After you ask for an appeal, you will get a notice. It will explain in detail why your coverage should end.

## What an appeal could mean for your costs

- If the independent reviewer agrees that your coverage should end, neither Medicare nor your plan will pay for services after March 14, 2025.
- If you stop services by March 14, 2025, you will not have to pay for them.

## How to ask for an immediate appeal

- **Ask as soon as you can.**
- To be on time, you must ask by **noon on Thursday, March 13, 2025**. That is the day before your coverage ends.
- Make your request to your Quality Improvement Organization (QIO). The QIO is the independent reviewer that Medicare has approved.
- If you miss the deadline, you may still have appeal rights.
- To appeal, or if you have questions, call the QIO:
  **Midsouth Quality Review: 1-888-555-0142**

## What happens next

- The QIO will tell you its decision as soon as it can. This is usually no later than two days after March 14, 2025.
- If you are in a Medicare health plan, the QIO usually tells you its decision by March 14, 2025.
- To learn more, call Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142.

## Sign and date below

Sign to show that you got this notice and understand it.

"I have been told that my coverage will end on the date on this notice. I know I can appeal by contacting my QIO."

Signature of patient or representative: ____________________

Date: ____________________

## Your rights

- You have the right to get this information in a format you can use. This includes large print, Braille, or audio.
- You have the right to file a complaint if you feel you were treated unfairly because of who you are (discrimination).
- To learn more, visit Medicare.gov/about-us/accessibility-nondiscrimination-notice. You can also call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227).
- If you use a TTY, call 1-877-486-2048.

# Your 2018 tax refund is on hold

We are holding your 2018 tax refund. We are reviewing your tax return to make sure it is correct.

## Why we picked your return

We want to check some things you may have reported. These may include:

- Income
- Income tax withholding
- Tax credits
- Business income

## What you need to know

- We may contact you or your authorized representative if we have questions.
- We may also contact other people or groups (third parties) to check information. We can only share what we must to check what we need.
- We have to keep a list of the third parties we contact. You can ask for a copy of that list. To ask, call 800-829-1040. Or write to the address at the top of this notice.

## What to do if you filed the tax return

**You do not need to do anything now.** We know your refund matters to you. We will finish the review as fast as we can.

**How long it may take**
- The review could take up to 60 days from the date of this notice (April 30, 2019).
- Please do not contact us before 60 days have passed. Until then, we cannot give you any more information.

**Check your refund status**
- Go to www.irs.gov/refunds.
- Or use the IRS2Go app on your smartphone.

**What happens after the review**
We may do one of these things:
- Send your refund.
- Ask you for more information.
- Deny all or part of your refund.

If we deny part or all of your refund and you do not agree, you can appeal.

**If 60 days pass and you have no refund or word from us**
Call us at 800-829-1040.

## What to do if you did NOT file the tax return

Someone may have used your personal information to try to get a tax refund. Please do these things:

- Fill out Form 14039, Identity Theft Affidavit. Send it with a copy of this notice. Mail it to the address in the Form 14039 instructions.
- Tell your banks and other financial institutions.
- Call the fraud department at one of the three big credit bureaus. The one you call will tell the other two.
  - Equifax: 800-525-6285, www.equifax.com
  - Experian: 888-397-3742, www.experian.com
  - TransUnion: 800-680-7289, www.transunion.com
- Report any fraud to your local police or sheriff's office.
- File a complaint with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). You can go to www.identitytheft.gov. Or call 877-438-4338.
- Learn about identity theft involving Social Security numbers. Go to the Social Security Administration website at www.ssa.gov/pubs/10064.html. Or call 800-772-1213.
- Visit www.irs.gov/ID for more information.

## More information

- Notice information: www.irs.gov/cp05
- Tax forms, instructions, and publications: go to www.irs.gov/forms-pubs. Or call 800-TAX-FORM (800-829-3676).
- To write to us, use the address at the top of this notice. Be sure to include:
  - Your Social Security number
  - The tax year you are writing about
  - The form number you are writing about
- **Keep this notice for your records.**

If you need help, please contact us.

Dear John and Mary Smith,

This letter is about your 2017 taxes.

**You owe $1,075.21**

Our records show that you still owe money on your 2017 tax return (Form 1040). The amount includes unpaid taxes, penalties, and interest.

If you paid the full amount in the last 21 days, or you already set up a payment plan, you can ignore this letter. If you already have a payment plan, keep following it.

**How we got this amount**
- Tax you owed: $3,183.00
- Payments and credits you already made: minus $3,328.00
- Late filing penalty: $318.30
- Late payment penalty: $633.30
- Interest: $145.00
- Penalty for not paying estimated tax: $123.61
- Total you still owe by February 20, 2018: $1,075.21

**If you agree with the amount**

Pay $1,075.21 by February 20, 2018. If you wait, you will owe more in penalties and interest.

- **Pay online** at www.irs.gov/payments. You can pay for free from your checking or savings account. You get a confirmation right away, and you can schedule a payment ahead of time or cancel it before the due date. You can also pay by debit or credit card for a small fee.
- **Pay by mail.** Write a check or money order to "United States Treasury." On it, write your Social Security number, "2017," and "Form 1040." Send it with the payment stub to: Internal Revenue Service, Cincinnati, OH 45999-0149.

**If you disagree with the amount**

Call 1-800-829-1040 to talk with a representative. Have your account information ready when you call. If we do not hear from you, we will assume you agree with this letter.

**If you cannot pay the full amount**

- **Payment plan:** Pay as much as you can now, and make arrangements to pay the rest. Visit www.irs.gov/paymentplan or call 1-800-829-1040.
- **Offer in Compromise:** You may be able to settle your tax debt for less than you owe. To see if you qualify, use the Offer in Compromise Pre-Qualifier tool at www.irs.gov/offers.

**Other information**

- To check your current balance or payment history, go to www.irs.gov/balancedue.
- If you think we made a mistake, call 1-800-829-1040 to review your account.
- If you are in a bankruptcy case, this letter is for your information only. It does not ask you to pay outside the bankruptcy process. You will not get another balance notice while the bankruptcy protection is in effect.

If we do not hear from you, please pay $1,075.21 by February 20, 2018, to avoid penalties and interest.

# Notice CP14: You Owe Money for Tax Year 2017

**From:** Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
**Notice date:** January 30, 2018
**Form:** 1040
**Tax year:** 2017
**Phone:** 1-800-829-1040

**To:** John and Mary Smith, 123 N Harris St, Harvard, TX 12345

## The main point

You owe **$1,075.21**. Our records show you have unpaid taxes, penalties, and interest on your 2017 Form 1040.

**Pay by February 20, 2018.**

## Do you need to pay?

You can ignore this notice if either of these is true:
- You already paid in full within the last 21 days.
- You already made payment arrangements.

If you already have an installment or payment agreement for this tax year, keep following that agreement.

## How we figured the amount

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Tax you owed | $3,183.00 |
| Payments and credits already applied | -$3,328.00 |
| Failure-to-file penalty | $318.30 |
| Failure-to-pay penalty | $633.30 |
| Interest charges | $145.00 |
| Failure-to-pay estimated tax penalty | $123.61 |
| **Amount due by February 20, 2018** | **$1,075.21** |

## If you are in bankruptcy

If you are a debtor in a bankruptcy case, this notice is only for your information. We are not trying to collect taxes you owed before you filed your bankruptcy petition. We are not asking for payment outside of the bankruptcy process.

You will not get another balance due notice while the automatic stay is in effect.

## What to do right away

**If you agree with the amount and you are not working with an IRS representative:**

1. Pay **$1,075.21** by **February 20, 2018**. This helps you avoid more penalty and interest charges.
2. Pay online or mail a check or money order with the payment stub. You can pay online now at www.irs.gov/payments.
3. Make your check or money order payable to the **United States Treasury**.
4. Write your Social Security number (nnn-nn-nnnn), the tax year (2017), and the form number (1040) on your payment.
5. Mail your payment to:
   Internal Revenue Service
   Cincinnati, OH 45999-0149

**Payment stub:** Amount due by February 20, 2018: $1,075.21.

**If you disagree with the amount:**

- Call us at **1-800-829-1040**. A representative will review your account with you.
- Have your account information ready when you call.

**If we don't hear from you,** we will assume you agree with this notice.

**If you think we made a mistake,** call 1-800-829-1040 and we will review your account.

## Ways to pay

### Pay online now
- We offer free ways to pay straight from your checking or savings account.
- When you pay online or with a mobile device, you can:
  - Get instant confirmation that we got your payment.
  - Schedule payments ahead of time.
  - Reschedule or cancel a payment before the due date.
- You can also pay by debit or credit card. There is a small fee.
- To see all payment options, go to www.irs.gov/payments.

### Payment plans
- If you can't pay the full amount, pay as much as you can now. Then make arrangements to pay the rest.
- You can set up an installment agreement or an online payment agreement. Learn more at www.irs.gov/paymentplan.
- You can also call us at 1-800-829-1040 to talk about your options.

### Offer in compromise
- An offer in compromise may let you settle your tax debt for less than the full amount you owe.
- If we accept your offer, you can pay with a lump sum cash payment or a periodic payment plan (payments over time).
- To see if you qualify, use the Offer in Compromise Pre-Qualifier tool on our website.
- For more information, go to www.irs.gov/offers.

### Account balance and payment history
To learn how to get your current account balance or payment history, go to www.irs.gov/balancedue.

## Remember

If you already paid in full within the last 21 days or made payment arrangements, you can ignore this notice.

## If we don't hear from you

Pay $1,075.21 by February 20, 2017, to avoid penalty and interest charges.

**Note:** This last line of the original notice says February 20, **2017**. Everywhere else, the notice says February 20, **2018**. The dates do not match. The 2018 date is the one used in the rest of the notice. You may want to call 1-800-829-1040 to confirm the correct due date.

text:
Dear Carla Jimenez,

This letter is about your 2017 Form 1040. This is the main form people use to file their federal income tax return.

**The IRS has no record that you filed your 2017 tax return.**

**What to do right away**

If you had to file a tax return for 2017, file it now. You can:

- Fill out your return using your current address. Sign it. If you owe taxes, include a payment. Mail it in the envelope we sent.
- File online through an e-file provider. This only works if it is within 2 years of the original due date.
- Pay online at www.irs.gov/payments. You can also mail a payment with your return.

**If you don't think you had to file a return for 2017**

Fill out the enclosed Form 15103, Form 1040 Return Delinquency. It asks whether any of the reasons on the form apply to you. Mail it with the bottom part of this letter (the stub) in the envelope we sent. You can also fax it to 1-855-555-0161. Tell us:

- Whether you already filed a 2017 return. If you did, send us a signed and dated copy of it with Form 15103.
- Whether you don't think you have to file, and which reason on Form 15103 applies.

**If we don't hear from you**

- If you don't file a return, or you think this letter is a mistake and you don't respond, you may owe penalties and interest on the taxes you owe. These charges can keep growing.
- You could lose your refund. If you are owed a refund for taxes taken out of your pay or paid ahead of time, you must file a return to get it. The deadline was April 15, 2021, plus any extension. The same rule applies to tax credits you may qualify for, such as the Earned Income Credit.
- If you earned interest or dividends and don't file or pay what you owe, the IRS can tell banks and other payers to keep some of your payments. That money goes to the IRS. You can claim it on your tax return later.

**What happens next**

We will contact you again if:

- We need more information about your tax return.
- We decide that you do need to file a 2017 return.

If you think we made a mistake, call 1-800-555-0137 to review your account.

**More information**

- Visit www.irs.gov/cp59.
- For tax forms, instructions, and publications, visit www.irs.gov or call 800-829-3676.
- To get your wage and income information, visit www.irs.gov/transcript.
- Keep this letter for your records.

If you need help, please contact us.

Sincerely,
Internal Revenue Service

Fresno, CA 93888-0025

## We have no tax return from you for 2017

Our records show that you did not send us a tax return (Form 1040) for 2017.

## What to do right now

If you had to file a tax return for 2017, please file it now. You can do this in one of three ways:

- **By mail:** Fill out your tax return. Use the address where you live now. Sign it. Add a payment if you owe taxes. Mail it to us in the envelope we sent.
- **By computer:** You can file online with an e-file company. You can only do this if it has been less than 2 years since the date your return was first due.
- **Pay online:** Go to www.irs.gov/payments. Or, you can mail a payment with your return.

## If you think you did not have to file

Fill out the form we sent, called Form 15103. It asks questions to find out if you needed to file. Send it back in one of two ways:

- Mail it with the bottom part of this notice in the envelope we sent.
- Fax it to 1-855-555-0161.

On the form, tell us if either of these is true:

- **You already filed a 2017 tax return.** If so, send us a copy of the return. Sign it and write the date on it. Send it with Form 15103.
- **You do not have to file.** The form lists the reasons a person might not need to file. Pick the one that fits you.

## What happens if you don't answer

- **You may owe extra money.** If you do not file, you may be charged penalties and interest on the tax you owe. This is also true if you think we sent this notice by mistake and you do not tell us. The extra charges can keep growing until you pay.
- **You could lose your refund.** A refund is money we give back to you if you paid too much during the year. If you are owed a refund, you must file your return to get it. The last day to ask for it is April 15, 2021. If you get more time to file, that date may be later. This is also true for tax credits that can give you money back, like the Earned Income Credit.
- **Some of your bank interest could be taken.** Say you earned interest or dividends (money from a bank or from investments). If you do not file or do not pay what you owe, the IRS may tell the places that pay you to hold back part of that money. They would send that money to the IRS. You can then count it as money you already paid when you file your return.

## What happens next

We will contact you again if:

- We need more information about your tax return.
- We decide that you did have to file a 2017 tax return.

If you think we made a mistake, call us at 1-800-555-0137. We will look at your account.

## More help

- Go to www.irs.gov/cp59.
- To get tax forms and help guides, go to www.irs.gov or call 1-800-829-3676.
- To get a record of your wages and income, go to www.irs.gov/transcript.
- Please keep this letter for your records.

If you need help, please contact us.

We are checking your 2016 tax return. This is called an audit. We need you to send us papers that prove the things you wrote on your return.

What you need to do right away

We are keeping part of your refund for now. We are holding back the Earned Income Credit (EIC) and/or the Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC). If you asked for the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), we may also hold back all or some of your refund because something does not match.

1. Fill out the Response form. Mail it or fax it to us with your papers. You must do this within 30 days from the date of this letter.
2. Send copies of papers that prove the items listed below. Send copies, not your only copies.
3. If you cannot get your papers ready in time, call us at 1-866-555-0188.

If we do not hear from you within 30 days, we will say no to the items we are checking. You may then owe more tax.

What we are checking and what to send

We need papers for these items:

Earned Income Credit (EIC)
- Read the enclosed form 886-H-EIC. It lists the papers you need to send.
- Send papers that prove your child meets these rules: the child is related to you, the child is the right age, and the child lived with you.

Premium Tax Credit (PTC)
- Read the enclosed form 14950. It explains this credit.
- Send papers that prove you have the right to this credit.

Filing Status (Head of Household)
- Read the enclosed form 886-H-HOH. It lists the papers you need.
- Send papers that prove you were the head of your household.

What happens next

- We will look at the papers you send. Please allow at least 30 days.
- If your papers prove your return is correct, we will send your refund. We will also send a letter saying the audit is finished.
- If your papers do not fully prove your return is correct, we will send you an audit report. This report will explain the changes we want to make. It may say you owe more tax, plus penalties and interest.

More information

- Visit www.irs.gov/cp75 to learn more.
- Read the enclosed Publication 3498-A. It explains the audit process and how you can appeal, which means asking for a second review if you disagree.
- Read the enclosed Publication 1. It explains your rights as a taxpayer.
- For tax forms and instructions, visit www.irs.gov/forms-pubs or call 800-829-3676.
- Keep this letter for your records.

If you need help, call us. We are glad to help.

We wrote to you before. Our records show you still have unpaid taxes for the tax year that ended December 31, 2016 (Form 1040A).

**Pay $9,533.53 by January 29, 2018.** If you don't, the interest will go up. More penalties may also apply.

## What you owe

- Amount you owed: $9,444.07
- Failure-to-pay penalty (already added): $34.98
- Interest (already added): $54.48
- **Total due by January 29, 2018: $9,533.53**

If you already have an installment or payment agreement for this tax year, keep following that agreement.

## What to do now

**If you agree with the amount due and you are not working with an IRS representative:**

- Pay $9,533.53 by January 29, 2018. This keeps you from paying more interest and penalties.
- You can pay online at www.irs.gov/payments. Or you can mail a check or money order with the payment stub that came with this letter.
- Make your check or money order payable to the **United States Treasury**.
- On your payment, write:
  - your social security number (NNN-NN-NNNN)
  - the tax year (2016)
  - the form number (1040A)

**Payment stub:** Amount due by January 29, 2018: $9,533.53.
Mail to: Internal Revenue Service, Cincinnati, OH 4599-0149.

**If we told you we paused collection because it would cause a financial hardship:** This means you could not pay basic living costs if we took money from you. If your money situation has not changed, you don't need to do anything.

**If you disagree with the amount due:**

- Call us at 1-800-829-1040. A representative will review your account with you.
- Have your account information ready when you call.
- If we don't hear from you, we will assume you agree with this notice.

## If you can't pay all of it

- Pay as much as you can now.
- Then make a plan to pay the rest.
- To learn about installment agreements and online payment agreements, go to www.irs.gov/paymentplan. You can also call 1-800-829-1040 to talk about your options.

## Other things to know

- If you already paid the full amount in the past 21 days, or you made payment arrangements, ignore this notice.
- If you think we made a mistake, call 1-800-829-1040. We will review your account.

## If we don't hear from you

Pay $9,533.53 by January 29, 2018. This keeps you from paying more interest and penalties.

If we don't hear from you, we may file a Notice of Federal Tax Lien against you.

- A tax lien usually covers all the property you own now. It will also cover any property you get in the future.
- The Notice of Federal Tax Lien is a public record.
- It can hurt your credit. It can also make it hard for you to get credit, such as a loan or a credit card.

**Questions? Call 1-800-829-1040.**

## We are checking your 2016 tax return

We need you to send us papers that prove what you reported.

Dear Tasha Greene,

We are checking (auditing) your 2016 tax return (Form 1040). We need you to send us papers that back up some of the things you claimed.

## What you need to do right away

We are holding part of your refund until the audit is done. This is the part for:

- the Earned Income Credit (EIC)
- the Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC)

If you claimed the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), we may also hold some or all of your refund. This is because the numbers for your PTC did not match.

Please do these things:

1. Fill out the Response form.
2. Mail or fax the form to us, along with copies of your papers. **You must do this within 30 days of the date on this letter (January 28, 2019).**
3. Send copies of papers that prove the items listed below.
4. If you can't get your papers ready in time, call us at 1-866-555-0188.

**Important:** If you do not answer within 30 days, we will not allow the items we are checking. You may then owe more tax.

## What we are checking and what to send

Look at each item below. Follow the steps to see what to send.

**1. Earned Income Credit**
- Read the form we included: Form 886-H-EIC. It lists the papers you need to send to claim this credit for a child.
- Send papers that show your child:
  - is related to you,
  - meets the age rule, and
  - lived with you for the required time.

**2. Premium Tax Credit**
- Read the form we included: Form 14950, Premium Tax Credit Verification.
- Send the papers it asks for. They should show you are allowed to claim this credit.

**3. Your filing status (Head of Household)**
- Read the form we included: Form 886-H-HOH. It lists papers that prove you are the head of your household.
- Send the papers it asks for. They should show you are the head of your household.

## What happens if we do not hear from you

If you do not mail or fax your papers within 30 days, we will not allow the items we are checking. We will then send you an audit report. It will show the changes we plan to make to your tax return.

## What happens next

- We will look at the papers you send. Please give us at least 30 days.
- **If your papers back up your tax return:** We will send your refund. We will also send a letter saying your audit is over.
- **If your papers do not fully back up your tax return:** We will send you an audit report. It will explain the changes we want to make. It will also show any extra tax you may owe, plus any penalties and interest.

## More help

- Go to www.irs.gov/cp75.
- Read the papers we included. One is called The Examination Process (Publication 3498-A). It explains how you can appeal (disagree with) our decision.
- Read Publication 1, Your Rights as a Taxpayer. We included it too.
- To get tax forms and instructions, go to www.irs.gov/forms-pubs or call 800-TAX-FORM (800-829-3676).
- Keep this letter for your records.

If you need help, please contact us.

## What this letter is about

The IRS is auditing your 2016 Form 1040. An audit is a check of your tax return. You need to send papers that back up some items you claimed on it.

## What you need to do now

You have **30 days from the notice date** to respond. The notice date is January 28, 2019.

1. Fill out the Response form.
2. Mail or fax the form to the IRS. Send it with your documents.
3. Include copies of papers that support the audit items listed below.

**Can't get your papers ready in time?** Call the IRS at **1-866-555-0188**. Call only if you can't get your documents ready in time.

## Your refund is on hold

The IRS is holding part of your refund until the audit is done. The held parts are the Earned Income Credit (EIC) and/or the Additional Child Tax Credit (ACTC).

If you claimed the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), the IRS may also hold all or part of your refund. This is because something about your PTC does not match.

## What to send for each audit item

Look at each item below. Follow the steps for it.

**Earned Income Credit (Form 1040)**
- Read the enclosed Form 886-H-EIC. Its full name is *Documents You Need to Send to Claim the Earned Income Credit on the Basis of a Qualifying Child or Children for Tax Year*.
- Send the papers it asks for. They must show that your child met the relationship, age and residency tests. These tests decide if you qualify for the credit.

**Premium Tax Credit (Form 1040)**
- Read the enclosed Form 14950, *Premium Tax Credit Verification*.
- Send the papers it asks for. They must show you are entitled to claim the Premium Tax Credit.

**Filing Status (Form 1040)**
- Read the enclosed Form 886-H-HOH, *Supporting Documents to Prove Head of Household Filing Status*.
- Send the papers it asks for. They must show you are the head of your household.

If you don't mail or fax your papers within 30 days of the notice date:
- The IRS will disallow the items being audited. That means the IRS will not allow them.
- You may owe more tax.
- The IRS will send you an audit report. It will show the changes the IRS proposes to make to your tax return.

## What happens next

The IRS will review what you send. Please allow at least 30 days.

- **If your papers support your tax return:** The IRS will send your refund. It will also send a letter saying your audit is closed.
- **If your papers don't fully support your tax return:** The IRS will send an audit report. It will explain the changes it proposes. It will show any extra tax you may owe. It will also show any penalties and interest that may apply.

## More information

- Go to **www.irs.gov/cp75**.
- Read the other papers that came with this notice.
- Read *The Examination Process* (Publication 3498-A). It explains your appeal rights.
- Read Publication 1, *Your Rights as a Taxpayer*. It is enclosed.
- For tax forms, instructions and publications, go to **www.irs.gov/forms-pubs**. You can also call **800-TAX-FORM (800-829-3676)**.
- **Keep this notice for your records.**

- IRS phone number on this notice: **800-829-1040**
- If your papers will be late: **1-866-555-0188**

## We plan to take your property, and you have the right to ask for a hearing

**You owe $4,823.12 right now.**

We sent you several notices about taxes you have not paid. We still have not gotten a payment from you. Because of this, the IRS can take your property, or your right to property, starting April 1, 2020. This is called a "levy." We could take:

- Your pay and other income
- Money in your bank accounts
- Business assets
- Personal items, including your car and home
- Your Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend and state tax refund
- Your Social Security benefits

## How we figured out what you owe

- Taxes you owed: $4,309.00
- Extra penalty charges: $399.96
- Extra interest charges: $114.16
- **Total you owe now: $4,823.12**

## How to pay

- Make your check or money order payable to the "United States Treasury."
- Write your Social Security number (nnn-nn-nnnn) on your payment and on anything else you send us.

## What you need to do now

**1. Pay what you owe.**
Send us $4,823.12. If you don't, we may take your property on or after April 1, 2020.

**2. If you can't pay it all, pay what you can and set up a plan.**
You can make a plan to pay the rest over time. To learn about your choices, go to www.irs.gov/payments or call us at 1-800-555-0153. Your choices include:
- Installment agreements (small payments over time)
- Automatic payments from your bank account
- Payments taken from your paycheck
- Credit card payments

**3. If you already paid, or think we missed a payment, send us proof.**
This could be a copy of a check or a receipt.

## You can ask for a hearing

If you disagree with our plan to take your property, you can ask for a hearing. This is called a Collection Due Process hearing. Here is how:

- Fill out the form that came with this letter. It is Form 12153.
- Mail it to the address at the top of this letter by **April 1, 2020**.
- Explain why you want a hearing. The form tells you where to do this (see section 8 and the instructions).
- Fill in the other information the form asks for.

**Important:** If you miss the April 1, 2020 deadline, you will lose your right to challenge the Appeals Office's decision in the U.S. Tax Court.

## About tax liens

A tax lien is a legal claim the government has on your property because you owe taxes.

- If you don't pay or call us to set up a plan, we can file a "Notice of Federal Tax Lien" at any time. We may have already done this.
- We can file this notice even if you ask for a hearing.
- The notice tells the people and companies you owe money to that the IRS has a claim on all your property. This includes property you get after the notice is filed.
- Once the notice is filed, it may show up on your credit report. It could hurt your credit score.
- The lien starts as soon as you miss paying your bill.
- The lien can't be removed until you pay everything you owe, including interest, penalties, and fees. It can also end if the time limit for us to collect the debt runs out.
- In some cases, the notice to your creditors can be withdrawn.

**If you have questions, call us at 1-800-555-0153.**

Dear Mr. Okafor:

This letter is about a change in your classes from September 1, 1996 on. Because of this change, we may have paid you more money than you should have gotten.

On November 5, 1996, you went from taking 12 credit hours to taking 6 credit hours.

### What We Did

On December 1, 1996, we lowered your payments to $202.00 a month. You will get another letter about this change. That letter will tell you if you owe us money.

### What We Need From You

Please send us a written statement that explains why you cut your credit hours from 12 to 6. In most cases, we need proof to back up your statement. ### When We Need It

Send us your statement and any proof within 30 days.

### What Will Happen Next

**If we accept your statement,** we will not lower your payments back to the start of the term. If you already owe us money, you must pay it back, but the amount will not go up.

**If we do not accept your statement and proof,** we will lower your payments starting September 1, 1996, the first day of the term. This means you will owe us money that you must pay back.

**If we do not hear from you within 30 days,** we will lower your payments starting September 1, 1996, the first day of the term. This means you will owe us money that you must pay back. Even so, we will still look at any information you send us within one year from the date of this letter. We may allow more time if you have a good reason why you could not send it in on time.

### Your Rights

You have basic rights before we make a final decision about your claim. Look at the enclosed paper called "Basic Rights" to learn more.

Sincerely,

**What we need from you**

- Send us a medical report from a doctor or clinic.

**Your right to privacy**

- Call us toll-free at **1-800-827-1000**.
- If you have trouble hearing, use our TDD number: **1-800-829-4833**.
- Please have this letter with you when you call.

Sincerely,

# Notice of Intent to Levy and Notice of Your Right to a Hearing

**This is a notice that the IRS plans to seize (levy) your property. It also tells you about your right to a Collection Due Process hearing. This is about overdue taxes.**

## Amount you must pay right now: $4,823.12

We sent you several notices about your overdue taxes. We have not received a payment.

On or after **April 1, 2020**, the IRS may seize (levy) your property or your rights to property. This can include:

- Your wages and other income
- Your bank accounts
- Your business assets
- Your personal assets, including your car and home
- Your Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend and state tax refund
- Your Social Security benefits

## What you owe

- Amount you originally owed: $4,309.00
- Additional penalty charges: $399.96
- Additional interest charges: $114.16
- **Total due right now: $4,823.12**

## What to do right now

**1. Pay the full amount.**
- Send us $4,823.12. If you don't, we may seize your property on or after April 1, 2020.
- Make your check or money order payable to the **United States Treasury**.
- Write your Social Security number on your payment. Also write it on anything else you send us.

**2. If you can't pay it all, pay what you can.**
- Pay as much as you can now.
- Then set up a plan to pay the rest over time.
- Your choices include payment plans (installment agreements), automatic deductions from your bank account, payroll deductions, and credit card payments.
- To learn more, go to **www.irs.gov/payments**.
- Or call us at **1-800-555-0153** to talk about your options.

**3. If you already paid, send proof.**
- Maybe you already paid your full balance. Or maybe you think we did not credit a payment to your account. If so, please send us proof of that payment.

## Your right to appeal: Collection Due Process hearing

You can appeal this plan to seize your property. To do that, ask for a Collection Due Process hearing.

- Fill out the enclosed **Form 12153**, *Request for a Collection Due Process or Equivalent Hearing*.
- Mail it by **April 1, 2020**.
- Send it to:
  Department of the Treasury
  Internal Revenue Service
  Philadelphia, PA 19255-0010
- On the form, give the reason you want a hearing. See section 8 of the form and the form's instructions.
- Also fill in the other information the form asks for.

**Important:** If you don't file Form 12153 by April 1, 2020, you lose the right to contest the Appeals decision in U.S. Tax Court.

## Federal tax liens

A tax lien is a legal claim against your property. Here is what you should know:

- If you don't pay, or don't call us to set up a payment plan, we can file a Notice of Federal Tax Lien at any time. We may have already done this.
- We can file the lien notice even if you ask for a hearing.
- The notice tells your creditors that the IRS has a claim against all your property. This includes property you get after the notice is filed.
- Once the notice is filed, it may show up on your credit report. It may hurt your credit rating.
- The lien itself starts once you have not paid your bill.
- The lien cannot be released until one of these happens:
  - You pay your bill in full, including interest, penalties, and fees.
  - The time the IRS has to legally collect the debt runs out.
- Under certain circumstances, the lien's notice to creditors may be withdrawn.

**Patient:** Eleanor Brooks
**Home health agency:** Riverbend Home Health
**Address:** 220 Hatcher Lane, Columbia, TN 38401
**Phone:** 931-555-0163

**What is changing?**
Starting April 7, 2025, you will get less physical therapy at home. Right now you get therapy 3 times each week. After April 7, you will get therapy 1 time each week.

**Why is this happening?**
Your therapist wrote down how you are doing. You can now walk 300 feet with a cane. You can also do your home exercises by yourself.

**Why did you get this letter?**
Your home health agency has decided to cut back on your therapy visits. This letter tells you about that choice.

**What if you think you still need more care?**
- You can look for a different home health agency. To do this, you must have a valid order for home care.
- If you need help finding another agency, call the doctor or provider who ordered your home care.
- If you use a different agency, you can ask them to bill Medicare.

**Where can you get help?**
- If you have questions, call your home health agency. You can also call the doctor or provider who ordered your care.
- You can only appeal to Medicare about payment if you actually get the care and a Medicare claim is sent in. An appeal means asking Medicare to take another look at a decision.

**Please sign this letter**
Your signature shows that you understand this letter. It does not mean you agree with the change.

Send the signed letter back to Riverbend Home Health. You can bring it in person or mail it to the address above.

- You can ask for this letter in a different form, such as large print, Braille, or audio.

Dear Mr. Pruitt,

This letter tells you why Medicare will stop paying for your care. It is not the answer to your appeal. If you appeal, a group called the Quality Improvement Organization (QIO) will make that decision.

**Why Medicare will stop paying**

We looked at your case. We decided Medicare should stop paying for your home health care.

**What we based this on:**
Your nurse visited you on March 3 and March 10, 2025. Her notes show that your surgery wound has closed. You do not need wound care every day anymore.

**Why this means coverage ends:**
Medicare pays for home health care only when you need a nurse or therapist to come to you from time to time. Now you or a caregiver can take care of your wound. So you no longer need a nurse for it.

The rule we used is in the Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 7, Section 40.1.

**Your health plan's rules:**

## Notice: Medicare May Not Pay for Your Test

Medicare does not pay for everything. Sometimes it won't pay even when you and your doctor think you need the care. If Medicare says no, you may have to pay the bill yourself.

**We think Medicare may not pay for this test:**

- **Test:** Vitamin D blood test
- **Why Medicare may not pay:** Medicare usually pays for this test only one time every 12 months.
- **What it may cost you:** $187.50

## What you need to do

1. Read this letter so you can make a good choice.
2. Ask us any questions you have.
3. Pick **one** of the three options below. Tell us if you still want the test. We can't pick for you.

If you pick Option 1 or Option 2, we may help you use other insurance you have. Medicare does not make us do this.

**Option 1: Yes, I want the test, and bill Medicare.**
- Medicare will look at the bill and make an official choice. You will get the answer in a letter called a Medicare Summary Notice (MSN).
- You can ask us to collect payment from you now.
- If Medicare says no, I have to pay. But I can appeal. That means I can ask Medicare to look again. The MSN will tell me how.
- If Medicare says yes, you will give back what I paid. I may still owe my co-pay or deductible.

**Option 2: Yes, I want the test, but do not bill Medicare.**
- You can ask me to pay now.
- I have to pay the whole cost.
- I cannot appeal, because Medicare is not being billed.

**Option 3: No, I do not want the test.**
- I do not have to pay anything.
- I cannot appeal, so I will not find out if Medicare would have paid.

## More information

This letter is only our opinion. It is not an official Medicare decision.

If you have questions about this letter or Medicare bills, call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227). If you use a TTY, call 1-877-486-2048.

## Your Rights as a Hospital Patient

- **Medicare pays for the care you need.** This includes hospital care that is medically needed. You have the right to know what Medicare pays for.
- **You can help plan your trip home.** Work with the hospital to make sure it is safe for you to leave. You can also set up any care you may need after you go home. If you are worried, talk to your doctor or the hospital staff.
- **You can report problems with your care.** Call the Quality Improvement Organization (a group that checks the quality of care):
  **Midsouth Quality Review: 1-888-555-0142**
  This group does not work for Medicare.

## You Can Appeal If You Are Told to Leave the Hospital

An appeal means you ask someone to take a second look at the decision.

- If you think you are being sent home too soon, you can appeal right away.
- To appeal, call **Midsouth Quality Review at 1-888-555-0142**.
- Try to call as soon as you can, and before you leave the hospital. If you call before you leave, Medicare will keep paying for your stay while you wait for the answer.
- If you appeal, Midsouth Quality Review will look at your health records. They will tell you their answer about 2 days after you ask.
- You can still appeal after you leave the hospital.
  - If you have **Original Medicare**, call Midsouth Quality Review.
  - If you have a **Medicare Advantage plan**, call your plan. Your plan is Volunteer Advantage Plan: **1-877-555-0175**.

## What Happens After I Appeal?

- If you appeal, you will get another letter called the **Detailed Notice of Discharge**. It tells you why the hospital thinks you no longer need to stay.
- If the answer is **yes** (in your favor), Medicare will keep paying for your hospital care.
- If you **do not appeal**, or if the answer is **no**, you may have to pay for care you get after your discharge date.

## Tax liens

A tax lien is a legal claim on your property. The lien starts when you do not pay your bill.

If you do not pay or call us to set up a plan, we can file a public notice of the lien. We may have done this already. We can file it even if you ask for a hearing.

Here is what a lien notice means for you:

- It tells the people and companies you owe money to that the IRS has a claim on everything you own.
- It also covers things you get after the notice is filed.
- It may show up on your credit report.
- It may hurt your credit score.

The lien stays until you pay your bill in full. That includes the interest, penalties, and fees. It can also end when the law no longer lets us collect the debt. In some cases, we can withdraw the public notice of the lien.

## Your 2017 Form 1040 tax return is missing

We have no record that you filed a Form 1040 tax return for the tax year that ended on December 31, 2017.

## What to do right now

**If you had to file a tax return for 2017, file it right away.** You can do it in one of these ways:

- **By mail:**
  - Use your current address.
  - Fill out your return and sign it.
  - Include a payment for any tax you owe.
  - Mail it to us in the envelope we sent.
- **By computer:** You can file through an e-file provider. You can only do this if it is within 2 years of the date the return was first due.
- **To pay:** You can pay online at www.irs.gov/payments. Or you can mail a payment with your return.

## If you don't think you had to file for 2017

Fill out the Form 15103 that came with this letter. Its name is "Form 1040 Return Delinquency." It asks if any of these apply to you.

Send us the form with the stub below. You can:
- Use the envelope we sent, or
- Fax it to 1-855-555-0161

On the form, tell us if:

- **You already filed a 2017 return.** If so, send us a copy of the return with your Form 15103. The copy must be signed and dated.
- **You don't think you have to file.** The form lists reasons. Pick the one that fits you.

## If you don't answer

- **You may owe more money.** Say you don't file, or you say this notice is wrong. If it turns out you owe tax, you may owe a penalty and interest on that tax. The penalty and interest may keep growing.
- **You could lose your refund.** If you don't file, you risk losing money owed to you. Say you are due a refund for taxes withheld or estimated taxes you paid. To get it, you must file your return by April 15, 2021. If you get more time to file, that extra time counts too. The same deadline applies to refundable tax credits, such as the Earned Income Credit.
- **Backup withholding could start.** This can happen only if you got interest or dividend income, and you don't file your return or don't pay all the tax you owe. Then the IRS will tell your payers (banks, for example) to hold back part of your dividend and interest payments. They send that money to the IRS. You can claim it as a withholding credit on your federal income tax return.

## What happens next

We will contact you again if:

- We need more information or a better explanation about your tax return, or
- We decide that you do need to file a 2017 return.

**If you think we made a mistake,** call 1-800-555-0137. We can look over your account with you.

## More help

- Notice information: www.irs.gov/cp59
- Tax forms, instructions and publications: go to www.irs.gov or call 800-TAX-FORM (800-829-3676).
- Wage and income transcript: you can ask for one at www.irs.gov/transcript.
- **Keep this notice for your records.**

If you need help, please contact us.
